lines.en: scene town2_noon
This Town Has Two Halves.
lines.zh: 这座小镇有两半。

lines.en: That's the name of the scene we get to talk about today.
lines.zh: 这就是我们今天要聊的那场戏的名字。

lines.en: And considering that this was (At least pre-revamp) one of the first moments in the game where things were hinted at being not quite what they seem, we have a bit of ground to cover.
lines.zh: 考虑到这（至少在改版前）是游戏里最早暗示「事情并不像表面那样」的时刻之一，我们有不少东西要讲。

lines.en: The day begins like any other.
lines.zh: 这一天像往常一样开始。

lines.en: World-renowned predator and all-around horrible guy, Sensei McSenseison [[ACTUAL NAME REDACTED AT THIS POINT IN TIME] is walking around with a boner or something.
lines.zh: 世界知名的掠食者、彻头彻尾的烂人 Sensei McSenseison[[真实姓名在此刻被隐去]正顶着勃起四处走动什么的。

lines.en: But for reasons beyond his comprehension and yours, he winds up here — in a section of Kumon-mi far detached from anything the reader has seen thus far.
lines.zh: 但出于他自己和你都无法理解的原因，他最后到了这里——Kumon-mi 的一个远离读者此前所见一切的区域。

lines.en: The feeling is different. There’s an immediate air of mystery as the monologue shifts to one closer to that of “Not Even Me,” an earlier event which, in several ways, serves as the precursor to this one.
lines.zh: 感觉不一样了。独白的语气立刻转向更接近《Not Even Me》那种神秘感——那是更早的一场事件，在好几个方面都是这一场的前身。

lines.en: And, in true self-indulgent Selebus fashion, the name of that event speaks volumes in telling the reader what is going on here.
lines.zh: 而且，以 Selebus 那套自我沉醉的一贯作风，那场事件的名字本身就已经向读者道尽了一切。

lines.en: For it’s not just the town that has two halves, it’s the protagonist. It’s the game. It’s the event. It’s {i}everything.{/i}
lines.zh: 因为有两半的不只是这座小镇，还有主角。还有游戏。还有这场事件。还有{i}一切{/i}。

lines.en: I’d been telling you from the start that things aren’t quite always as they seem, and the reason I spent so long forcing that into your head is-
lines.zh: 我从一开始就一直在告诉你，事情并不总是像表面那样，而我花那么久把这点硬塞进你脑子里，是因为——

lines.en: Well, sometimes you need to force things on people to move things forward.
lines.zh: 嗯，有时候你就是得把东西强加给别人，才能推动事情往前走。

lines.en: (That was not an endorsement of rape or sexual assault. Don’t rape or sexually assault anyone. That is a bad thing to do and I have to say this or people on the Internet will cry and misinterpret my words.)
lines.zh: （这不是在为强奸或性侵背书。不要强奸或性侵任何人。那是很坏的行为，我必须这么说，否则网上的人会哭闹着曲解我的话。）

lines.en: scene yumi4 with flash
: Yo! What the fuck?! I’ve been waiting here for like three hours!
lines.zh: : 喂！搞什么鬼？！我在这儿等了差不多三个小时了！

lines.en: : My bad, Yumi. I must have blacked out or some-
lines.zh: : 我的错，Yumi。我大概是昏过去了还是怎么——

lines.en: : Don’t give me that shit! If anybody here’s familiar with those bullshit blackout things, it’s me. You’re just a fucking prick.
lines.zh: : 少跟我扯这套！要说这儿谁最熟悉那种狗屁昏厥，那就是我。你就是个他妈的混蛋。

lines.en: : But I am a prick who {i}cares.{/i}
lines.zh: : 但我这个混蛋是{i}在乎的{/i}。

lines.en: scene yumi3
: If you {i}actually{/i} cared you’d compromise on your creative vision and make a version of the game that deaf people can play...
lines.zh: : 你要是{i}真的{/i}在乎，就该在创作理念上妥协，做一版聋人也能玩的游戏……

lines.en: Anyway...where were we?
lines.zh: 总之……我们说到哪儿了？

lines.en: Oh, right.
lines.zh: 哦，对了。

lines.en: Sexual assault is bad.
lines.zh: 性侵是坏事。

lines.en: But not only is it bad, it runs rampant in games like these as nothing short of fetish material and, while that isn’t a {i}problem{/i} in the confines of fiction, it’s not the direction I wanted to take my game in.
lines.zh: 但它不只是坏，它还在这类游戏里作为纯粹的癖好素材肆意泛滥；虽然这在虚构的范围内不{i}算问题{/i}，但那不是我想要的游戏方向。

lines.en: You’ll find out later just how important sexual trauma is in the grand scheme of things, but the major takeaway I wanted to leave with This Town Has Two Halves is that...
lines.zh: 你之后会知道性创伤在整体格局里有多重要，但我希望《这座小镇有两半》留给你的核心结论是……

lines.en: There are going to be things that happen in Lessons in Love that are beyond your control. And that goes for both the player {i}and{/i} that character players are being forced to follow.
lines.zh: 《Lessons in Love》里会有一些你无法掌控的事情发生。这对玩家{i}和{/i}玩家被迫跟随的那个角色都成立。

lines.en: scene yumi9 with flash
There are several ways I can spin this to make the message here more profound.
lines.zh: 我可以用好几种说法把这里的信息包装得更深刻。

lines.en: I can talk about how visual novels grant the illusion of freedom by giving you a couple checkboxes to make you feel like you’re actually contributing something to the story someone else is telling.
lines.zh: 我可以谈视觉小说如何用几个选项框给你自由的幻觉，让你觉得自己真在为别人讲的故事做点贡献。

lines.en: I can say that same thing about religion and how many schools of thought will gaslight you into believing you’re free to choose your own path before ostracizing you for doing so.
lines.zh: 我也可以把同样的话用在宗教上——多少思想流派会PUA你相信你可以自由选择自己的路，然后因为你真的这么做了而排斥你。

lines.en: I can tell you {i}anything{/i} and you will believe it because I am the one in control here.
lines.zh: 我可以说{i}任何话{/i}，而你都会相信，因为这里掌握主动权的是我。

lines.en: But it really all comes down to one singular idea that may or may not be true based on the last sentence I spoke to you.
lines.zh: 但归根结底，一切只归结为一个观念——而这个观念是真是假，取决于我上一句对你说的话。

lines.en: scene mothersmilk7 with flash
: Nothing you do matters.
lines.zh: : 你做的任何事都毫无意义。

lines.en: scene yumi12 with flash
Suffering can be beautiful when it’s choreographed in a way that gets the reader to think.
lines.zh: 当痛苦被编排得能让读者思考时，它也可以是美的。

lines.en: Anyone with half a brain would have realized something was {i}wrong{/i} the moment this event started — and I don’t mean “wrong” in the normal “Sensei is a predator” type of way.
lines.zh: 任何有点脑子的人在这场事件一开始就会意识到有{i}不对劲{/i}——我说的不是那种常见的「Sensei 是个掠食者」式的「不对劲」。

lines.en: I mean wrong in the fact that there is {i}something else{/i} at play here.
lines.zh: 我说的是这里还有{i}别的东西{/i}在起作用的那种不对劲。

lines.en: Could it be an invisible character hidden in the background? An unreliable narrator? Something the game itself is not telling you?
lines.zh: 会不会是藏在背景里的隐形角色？一个不可靠的叙述者？某种游戏本身没告诉你的东西？

lines.en: Could it be {i}all{/i} of those things?
lines.zh: 会不会{i}全都{/i}是？

lines.en: Or could this just be a meaningless showcase of sexual assault meant to appeal to those who downloaded this game not expecting to be shown the truer side of what that can do to a girl?
lines.zh: 还是说，这不过是一场毫无意义的性侵展示，用来讨好那些下载了这款游戏、却没料到会看到这种事对女孩真正意味着什么的人？

lines.en: This Town Has Two Halves is more than just a “main event” that winds up shaping the relationship of the two characters involved in it for the rest of the game.
lines.zh: 《这座小镇有两半》不只是一场「主线事件」——它最终塑造了其中两个角色在余下整个游戏里的关系。

lines.en: It’s {i}me{/i} taking {i}your{/i} face in {i}my{/i} hands and forcing {i}my{/i} tongue down {i}your{/i} throat as a way to get you to {i}see{/i} me.
lines.zh: 它是{i}我{/i}用{i}我{/i}的双手捧住{i}你{/i}的脸、把{i}我{/i}的舌头强塞进{i}你{/i}喉咙，只为让你{i}看见{/i}我。

lines.en: scene grass6 with flash
Tell me you see me.
lines.zh: 告诉我你看到的是我。

lines.en: scene yumi17 with flash
No matter how desperately you struggle to chip away at the block of cement that’s been hardening around your feet since the moment you came here, you’ll never break free.
lines.zh: 无论你多么拼命地想凿开那坨从你踏进这里的那一刻起就在你脚边凝固的水泥，你都永远挣脱不了。

lines.en: This whole journey is meant to submerge you in a sense of powerlessness so that, one day, you won’t {i}be{/i} powerless anymore.
lines.zh: 这整段旅程是为了让你彻底沉入无力感，好让你有朝一日{i}不再{/i}无力。

lines.en: You will grow — because that is what you’re designed to do.
lines.zh: 你会成长——因为那是你被设计出来要做的事。

lines.en: That is what you’re {i}all{/i} designed to do.
lines.zh: 那是{i}你们所有人{/i}被设计出来要做的事。

lines.en: And you should thank me for sticking my tongue down your throat because if I hadn’t, you wouldn’t be here.
lines.zh: 而你应该感谢我把舌头塞进你喉咙，因为要不是我那么做，你就不会在这儿。

lines.en: None of this would.
lines.zh: 这一切都不会存在。

lines.en: scene yumi19
I have an unlimited supply of pawns at my disposal and I am not afraid to fill my stomach with them as they keep my insides warm and make me feel full.
lines.zh: 我手上有取之不尽的棋子，而我不怕用它们填满我的胃——它们让我的内脏保持温暖，让我感到饱足。

lines.en: Do you like the inside of my stomach?
lines.zh: 你喜欢我胃里的样子吗？

lines.en: Does it make you feel warm as well?
lines.zh: 它是否也让你感到温暖？

lines.en: Or are you still just here to bathe in the misfortune of others so you don’t have to think too much about yourself?
lines.zh: 还是说你留在这儿只是为了泡在别人的不幸里，好不必太多地思考自己？

lines.en: scene black
It’s fine either way.
lines.zh: 哪种都无所谓。

lines.en: Wriggling your ivory bodies won’t free you from the hole you’ve fallen into.
lines.zh: 扭动你们那象牙色的身体，并不能让你们从掉进去的洞里脱身。

lines.en: It’ll just tickle my organs and remind me of how free {i}I{/i} am.
lines.zh: 它只会挠痒我的内脏，提醒我{i}我{/i}有多自由。

lines.en: You remind me of this every time you come back.
lines.zh: 你们每次回来，都在提醒我这一点。

lines.en: Thank you for making me full.
lines.zh: 谢谢你们让我吃饱。

lines.en: scene meintheroom2 with flash
: It is at this point that I will, once again, answer several questions submitted by the audience.
lines.zh: : 到这个时候，我又要再一次回答观众提交的几个问题。

lines.en: : {i}Question 1{/i}: Was TTHTH planned from the beginning, or was it something that came to you later on? And how did the community reaction differ from what you were expecting?
lines.zh: : {i}问题 1{/i}：TTHTH 是一开始就规划好的，还是后来才想到的？社区反应和你预期有多大差别？

lines.en: : Like most things, This Town Has Two Halves was {i}not{/i} planned from the beginning.
lines.zh: : 和大多数东西一样，《这座小镇有两半》{i}并不是{/i}一开始就规划好的。

lines.en: : Parts of it were as they directly related to the world I created, but I had no idea it would wind up existing in its current form as I don’t typically plan things out that way.
lines.zh: : 其中有些部分确实有，因为它们与我创造的世界直接相关，但我从没想过它最后会以现在这个形态存在——我通常不那样提前规划。

lines.en: : I like things to develop organically and this event just kind of happened where it happened and {i}how{/i} it happened because it...did.
lines.zh: : 我喜欢让东西自然生长，而这场事件就是发生在它发生的地方、以它发生的方式{i}发生{/i}了，因为它……就是发生了。

lines.en: : I can’t say why. Maybe I’m just a puppet on a string as well?
lines.zh: : 我说不出为什么。也许我自己也不过是个提线木偶？

lines.en: : In terms of the community reaction, I don’t remember much as that was nearly three years ago at this point.
lines.zh: : 至于社区反应，我记不太清了，毕竟到现在已经快三年了。

lines.en: : But, to this day, I still get a little dopamine hit every time someone wonders if there was something they could have done to affect the outcome.
lines.zh: : 但直到今天，每当有人琢磨自己是不是本可以做点什么来改变结果时，我都会得到一点多巴胺快感。

lines.en: : {i}Question 2{/i}: As you were working on a story that was shaping up to be quite popular, throwing in content like this seems daunting...what effect did that have on you trying to make a career out of this?
lines.zh: : {i}问题 2{/i}：当你正在写一个逐渐变得相当受欢迎的故事时，插入这样的内容似乎很冒险……这对你想以此为业有什么影响？

lines.en: : That’s not really something I was thinking of. From the beginning, I’ve been focused on telling the story {i}I{/i} want to tell- not the story people want to hear. But I think that’s {i}why{/i} I’m successful.
lines.zh: : 那其实不是我会考虑的事。从一开始，我就专注于讲{i}我{/i}想讲的故事——而不是人们想听的故事。但我觉得这正是{i}为什么{/i}我能成功。

lines.en: : You’ll never succeed by just doing what everyone else does and there is no purpose at all in creativity if you’re just going to let others wash that away when it makes them feel uncomfortable.
lines.zh: : 光做别人都在做的事，你永远不会成功；而如果你的创造力一让别人不舒服就被冲掉，那它根本毫无意义。

lines.en: : {i}Question 3{/i}: As one of the first “more distressing” events in the game, what was the reason for having it happen in a new area away from the school and other previously-available places?
lines.zh: : {i}问题 3{/i}：作为游戏里最早「更令人不适」的事件之一，为什么让它发生在一个远离学校和其他此前可去之处的新区域？

lines.en: : Having it happen somewhere else was the {i}whole point{/i} as it was me showing the reader that there is always another darker world pressed beneath a brighter one.
lines.zh: : 让它发生在别处正是{i}重点所在{/i}，因为那是我在向读者展示：在更明亮的世界之下，总压着另一个更黑暗的世界。

lines.en: : Confining a huge moment like this to somewhere players were already familiar with wouldn’t have gotten the same level of grandiose confusion across.
lines.zh: : 把这样重大的时刻限制在玩家已经熟悉的地方，就无法传达出同等程度的宏大困惑感。

lines.en: : People needed to see firsthand just how little they knew about the world the game was taking place in.
lines.zh: : 人们需要亲眼看到，他们对游戏所在的那个世界了解得有多浅。

lines.en: : In my mind, the most effective way of doing that was dropping them into an area they had zero knowledge of before taking even {i}more{/i} of their power away.
lines.zh: : 在我看来，最有效的做法就是把他们丢进一个他们一无所知的区域，再夺走他们{i}更多{/i}的掌控权。

lines.en: : I wanted you to feel as lost and alone as possible.
lines.zh: : 我想让你尽可能感到迷失与孤独。

lines.en: : {i}Question 4{/i}: Was the purpose behind Yumi “kissing back” to allow an exploration of the moral/psychological internal struggle faced by survivors of abuse?
lines.zh: : {i}问题 4{/i}：让 Yumi「回吻」的目的，是为了探讨受虐幸存者所面临的道德／心理内部挣扎吗？

lines.en: : For the most part, yes. Being in a situation like that, where you have no means of escaping and must either give in or fight a battle that could only end in failure and further harm is {i}terrifying.{/i}
lines.zh: : 大体上是。身处那种境地——无处可逃，只能屈服、或者打一场注定失败且会带来更大伤害的仗——是{i}极其恐怖的{/i}。

lines.en: : But there’s an added layer of hormone-based confusion that I wanted to be relevant in the scene as well.
lines.zh: : 但我想让这一场里还有一层由激素带来的困惑也发挥作用。

lines.en: : Yumi’s a teenage girl who had been too busy struggling with authority to ever really face or accept the parts of herself that {i}everyone{/i} her age must eventually deal with.
lines.zh: : Yumi 是个少女，她一直忙于与权威抗争，以至于从没真正面对或接受她这个年纪{i}每个人{/i}最终都必须处理的那部分自己。

lines.en: : So for a brief moment in time, even if that moment came well before it should have and without her consent, she was forced to confront that and {i}feel{/i} the things she’d successfully avoided thus far.
lines.zh: : 于是在短暂的一刻里——哪怕这一刻来得远远太早、且未经她同意——她被迫直面并{i}感受{/i}了她此前一直成功回避的东西。

lines.en: : She was surrendering to not only the actions of someone older, larger, and more powerful than her- but to the wanton, subconscious craving to be desired that she was never able to fully understand.
lines.zh: : 她屈服的不只是某个比她年长、更高大、更有力的人的行为——还有那种她始终无法完全理解的、肆意而潜意识的「渴望被渴望」。

lines.en: : {i}Question 5{/i}: As someone who is heavily disgusting by the use of rape as a porn tag, I may have dropped the game right there. Was that something you considered when writing this event?
lines.zh: : {i}问题 5{/i}：作为一个极度厌恶把强奸当作色情标签的人，我可能当场就弃游了。你写这场事件时考虑过这一点吗？

lines.en: : No, I really don’t give a shit about what people {i}do{/i} or {i}don’t{/i} want to see.
lines.zh: : 没有，我真他妈不在乎人们{i}想{/i}还是{i}不想{/i}看什么。

lines.en: : I wouldn’t use disgusting scenarios like that if I didn’t want people to {i}be disgusted.{/i} Getting them to quit just means I did my job well and impacted them in a meaningful way.
lines.zh: : 如果我不想让人{i}感到恶心{/i}，我就不会用那种恶心的场景。让他们弃游只说明我把活儿干好了，并且真正有意义地影响了他们。

lines.en: : {i}Final Question{/i}: Why give the reader a choice at all if both choices lead to the same place?
lines.zh: : {i}最后一个问题{/i}：既然两个选项通向同一个结果，为什么还要给读者选择？

lines.en: : This was touched on earlier, but the easy way of putting it would be, “I wanted them to feel like they had some sort of influence on the game.”
lines.zh: : 前面提过一点，最简单的说法是：「我想让他们觉得自己对游戏有某种影响力。」

lines.en: : While there are paths you can take with the characters that help sculpt interpersonal relationships in different ways, that’s not what this event is about.
lines.zh: : 虽然你可以和角色走出不同路线、以不同方式塑造人际关系，但那不是这场事件的重点。

lines.en: : This Town Has Two Halves, even if it played a monumental role in Yumi’s subsequent characterization, is about {i}the world.{/i} It’s not about Yumi. {i}That{/i} is why you couldn’t change anything.
lines.zh: : 《这座小镇有两半》虽然对 Yumi 之后的人物塑造起了重大作用，但它讲的是{i}这个世界{/i}。不是 Yumi。{i}这{/i}就是你什么都改变不了的原因。

lines.en: : The player can not contest what the game itself {i}wants{/i} you to do — nor would Sensei even have the agency or drive at this point in time to fight back.
lines.zh: : 玩家无法对抗游戏本身{i}想要{/i}你做的事——而且在这个时间点，Sensei 连反抗的能动性或动力都没有。

lines.en: : Giving players two choices that result in the same tragedy is a powerful tool to make them scramble and think for a moment that they did something wrong.
lines.zh: : 给玩家两个通向同一场悲剧的选项，是一种强有力的手段，让他们慌乱地以为自己做了什么错事。

lines.en: : The thing is, though...they did.
lines.zh: : 可问题在于……他们确实做错了。

lines.en: : It is {i}the player{/i} who decided to press on in a game about fucking high schoolers.
lines.zh: : 是{i}玩家{/i}决定继续玩一款操高中生的游戏。

lines.en: : It is {i}the player{/i} who sought reprieve in a genre so typically tone-deaf that the real-world implications of its contents has been all but abandoned.
lines.zh: : 是{i}玩家{/i}在一个通常如此麻木不仁、以至于其内容的现实意义早已被弃之不顾的类型里寻求慰藉。

lines.en: : If you want to hide from that, do it...but there is no room to hide here.
lines.zh: : 如果你想逃避这一点，那就逃吧……但这里没有藏身之处。

lines.en: : Here, you will be punished for simply watching- because watching makes you complicit.
lines.zh: : 在这里，你仅仅因为观看就会受到惩罚——因为观看让你成为共犯。

lines.en: : And if you truly cared at all, you’d have taught yourself to look away.
lines.zh: : 而你要是真的在乎，就该学会移开目光。
